content.rendered:
While Moses’ hands stayed raised, Israel prevailed over Amalek. Afterward, he built an altar and named it Jehovah Nissi, the Lord Is My Banner.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, August 14, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And Moses built an altar and called its name, The-LORD-Is-My-Banner.”
Exodus 17:15 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Amalek attacked Israel without warning, and Moses sent Joshua into the valley to fight while he climbed a hill with Aaron and Hur. As long as Moses held his hands up, Israel prevailed. When his arms grew tired and dropped, Amalek began to prevail instead. So Aaron and Hur did something simple and decisive: they held his hands up until the sun went down, and Israel won the battle (Exodus 17:8-13).

What Moses named afterward was not a strategy. It was not “the Lord who taught us formation” or “the Lord who gave Joshua skill.” He called the altar Jehovah Nissi — the Lord is my banner, my standard, my rallying point. A banner in ancient warfare was not a weapon. It was the visible sign around which a scattered army regrouped, the flag a soldier looked for when the battle got confusing and he needed to know which side he belonged to and where to stand.

The Amplified Bible expands the picture: “Moses built an altar and named it The Lord Is My Banner [Yahweh-Nissi]” (Exodus 17:15 AMP). The victory was won in the valley by Joshua’s sword, but it was sustained on the hill by raised hands fixed on God. That is the pattern of every real spiritual victory: the fight happens where you are, but the outcome is tied to what you are looking at while you fight.

Notice, too, that Moses did not raise his hands alone the whole day. When he grew tired, Aaron and Hur held his arms up for him. Jehovah Nissi’s banner is not only a personal rallying point — it is a shared one. Part of walking in this name is recognising when your own strength is failing and letting someone else hold your arms up until the sun goes down on your battle.

If you are in a valley today — fighting a battle you did not choose, against an enemy that came without warning — look up before you look around. Fix your eyes on the banner. And if your arms are tired, do not be ashamed to let someone else help hold them up.

Prayer

Father, You are Jehovah Nissi, my banner and my rallying point. When the battle is confusing and my strength is failing, let me fix my eyes on You and not on the size of the fight. Thank You for the people You have placed beside me to hold my hands up when I grow weary. Let me prevail today because my eyes are on You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My God is Jehovah Nissi, my banner. Whatever battle I face today, my eyes are fixed on Him, not on the size of the enemy. When my strength fails, He sends help to hold my hands up. I prevail because He is my rallying point.
